usage.callShape: GET https://laso.finance/get-card?amount=5&format=json (no body). x402 payment EQUALS the card value: amount=5 charges 5 USDC on Base (5000000 base units). Base USDC or Solana USDC accepted.
usage.outputShape: body.card.card_id (prepaid card id), body.card.usd_amount, body.card.status ("pending" at order time -> poll for funded), body.user_id (wallet that owns the card), body.callable_base_url (Firebase Functions host for follow-up card ops), body.auth.id_token (1h Firebase JWT bearer), body.auth.refresh_token, body.auth.expires_in
quirks: THE PRICE IS THE PRODUCT: the x402 charge equals the card value. amount=5 charges $5 USDC and loads a $5 card. amount is min $5 / max $1000 -> a higher amount means a higher real charge. Default/min is $5.
OUTWARD + IRREVERSIBLE: this actually creates and funds a real US prepaid debit card with real money. Get human approval before calling, and pick amount deliberately.
Pass &format=json so an agent gets JSON; default mimeType is text/html (browser view).

Card comes back status='pending' (card_id assigned, e.g. O-01KTN62GBAKT1VERAFMC962NYN). The actual card number/CVV/expiry are NOT in this response — you must poll/fetch them later using body.auth.id_token as a bearer token against body.callable_base_url.
auth.id_token is a 1h Firebase JWT; use auth.refresh_token to renew before it expires.
US-only; prepaid cards are not accepted at all merchants. Use the merchant-acceptance search before relying on it.
The card and token are bound to the paying wallet (user_id 0xdd13...). No separate sign-in/SIWX needed for this call; x402 payment alone authenticates and identifies you.
Registry surface lists this as a $5.00 endpoint at GET /get-card — correct, but note the $5 is the minimum card value, not a fixed service fee.
usage.guide: Call GET https://laso.finance/get-card?amount=N&format=json where N is the USD value you want on the card ($5-$1000). The x402 payment equals N USDC on Base (or Solana), so you are spending real money that lands on a real US prepaid debit card — always get explicit user approval and set amount intentionally. On 200, read body.card.card_id and body.card.status (status will be 'pending' at order time). The card number/CVV/expiry are not in this response: use body.auth.id_token as a Bearer token against body.callable_base_url (Firebase Cloud Functions) to fetch the funded card details, check balance, search merchant acceptance, or withdraw. This is outward and irreversible.
